questions.question: What mechanistic pathway explains the selective 1,4-addition of lithium dialkylcuprates (R₂CuLi) to conjugated enones?

options.label: A
options.text: Concerted [2+2] cycloaddition to form an oxetane.

options.label: B
options.text: Single-electron transfer and coordination of copper to the enone π system followed by migratory insertion at the β-carbon and reductive elimination.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct SN2 displacement at the carbonyl carbon.

options.label: D
options.text: Free radical abstraction of the carbonyl oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Single-electron transfer and coordination of copper to the enone π system followed by migratory insertion at the β-carbon and reductive elimination.
questions.explanation: Organocuprates are soft organometallic reagents that undergo oxidative addition/migratory insertion selectively at the softer β-carbon of enones.

questions.question: What is the reactive organometallic species in the Simmons-Smith cyclopropanation using CH₂I₂ and Zn(Cu)?

options.label: A
options.text: Iodomethylzinc iodide (ICH₂ZnI), a zinc carbenoid that transfers a methylene (:CH₂) unit stereospecifically syn across the alkene π bond.

options.label: B
options.text: A methyl radical and zinc iodide.

options.label: C
options.text: A cyclopropyl cation intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: Free singlet carbene in the gas phase.

questions.correct_answer: Iodomethylzinc iodide (ICH₂ZnI), a zinc carbenoid that transfers a methylene (:CH₂) unit stereospecifically syn across the alkene π bond.
questions.explanation: The zinc carbenoid delivers methylene via a concerted butterfly transition state without generating free carbene intermediates.

questions.question: How is dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) generated from chloroform (CHCl₃) and potassium tert-butoxide?

options.label: A
options.text: Deprotonation of the acidic C-H bond by tert-butoxide yields the trichloromethanide anion (⁻:CCl₃), which undergoes α-elimination by expelling a chloride ion.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-Cl bond by UV light.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct oxidation of chloroform by oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: Concerted elimination of two chlorine atoms simultaneously.

questions.correct_answer: Deprotonation of the acidic C-H bond by tert-butoxide yields the trichloromethanide anion (⁻:CCl₃), which undergoes α-elimination by expelling a chloride ion.
questions.explanation: Alpha-elimination involves loss of a proton and a halide from the same carbon atom, creating a neutral divalent carbon intermediate with a lone pair and empty p orbital.

questions.question: What is the correct sequential order of elementary steps in the palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling?

options.label: A
options.text: Reductive elimination → Migratory insertion → Beta-elimination.

options.label: B
options.text: Transmetalation → Oxidative addition → Reductive elimination.

options.label: C
options.text: Radical initiation → Propagation → Termination.

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidative addition of Pd(0) into aryl halide → Transmetalation of organoboronic acid to Pd(II) → Reductive elimination of biaryl product regenerating Pd(0).

questions.correct_answer: Oxidative addition of Pd(0) into aryl halide → Transmetalation of organoboronic acid to Pd(II) → Reductive elimination of biaryl product regenerating Pd(0).
questions.explanation: The Suzuki catalytic cycle comprises three core organometallic steps: oxidative addition, base-assisted transmetalation, and reductive elimination.

questions.topic: Suzuki Coupling Base Role in Transmetalation
questions.question: What is the crucial role of the base (e.g., Na₂CO₃ or NaOH) in the Suzuki-Miyaura coupling?

options.label: A
options.text: Base oxidizes Pd(0) to Pd(II).

options.label: B
options.text: Base precipitates palladium as a solid mirror.

options.label: C
options.text: Base deprotonates the aryl halide.

options.label: D
options.text: Base coordinates to the boron atom of the boronic acid to form an anionic boronate complex [Ar-B(OH)₃⁻], which activates the organic group for transmetalation to palladium.

questions.correct_answer: Base coordinates to the boron atom of the boronic acid to form an anionic boronate complex [Ar-B(OH)₃⁻], which activates the organic group for transmetalation to palladium.
questions.explanation: Neutral boronic acids undergo transmetalation very slowly; conversion to the negatively charged boronate complex dramatically accelerates transmetalation.

questions.topic: Heck Reaction Migratory Insertion and Syn Beta-Elimination
questions.question: In the Heck coupling of iodobenzene with methyl acrylate, what determines the trans alkene stereochemistry?

options.label: A
options.text: Backside SN2 attack of palladium on the double bond.

options.label: B
options.text: Radical coupling in solution.

options.label: C
options.text: Syn migratory insertion of the alkene into the Pd-Ar bond followed by C-C bond rotation and syn β-hydride elimination to form the thermodynamically favored trans-cinnamate.

options.label: D
options.text: Anti-elimination of palladium hydride.

questions.correct_answer: Syn migratory insertion of the alkene into the Pd-Ar bond followed by C-C bond rotation and syn β-hydride elimination to form the thermodynamically favored trans-cinnamate.
questions.explanation: Both migratory insertion and β-hydride elimination are strictly syn processes; internal rotation to align Pd and H syn delivers the trans-alkene.

questions.question: What is the fundamental transformation during the transmetalation step of a Stille cross-coupling?

options.label: A
options.text: Proton transfer from tin to palladium.

options.label: B
options.text: Transfer of an organic group from an organostannane (R-SnBu₃) to a Pd(II) complex with displacement of a halide ligand to form an R-Pd-R' intermediate.

options.label: C
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the C-Pd bond by tin radicals.

options.label: D
options.text: Oxidation of tin from Sn(II) to Sn(IV).

questions.correct_answer: Transfer of an organic group from an organostannane (R-SnBu₃) to a Pd(II) complex with displacement of a halide ligand to form an R-Pd-R' intermediate.
questions.explanation: Transmetalation exchanges the carbon nucleophile from tin to palladium without requiring strong base.

questions.question: Why is the Negishi coupling utilizing organozinc reagents (R-ZnX) exceptionally versatile in multi-step synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: Organozinc reagents are moderately reactive, undergoing rapid transmetalation with Pd(II) while tolerating diverse functional groups (esters, nitriles, ketones).

options.label: B
options.text: Zinc reagents are radioactive tracers.

options.label: C
options.text: Organozinc reagents never require transition metal catalysts.

options.label: D
options.text: Organozinc reagents are completely insoluble in all solvents.

questions.correct_answer: Organozinc reagents are moderately reactive, undergoing rapid transmetalation with Pd(II) while tolerating diverse functional groups (esters, nitriles, ketones).
questions.explanation: Organozinc compounds strike an ideal balance of functional group tolerance and transmetalation reactivity with palladium.

questions.question: What four-membered cyclic intermediate mediates carbon-carbon double bond rearrangement in Grubbs alkene metathesis?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: A metallacyclobutane intermediate formed by reversible [2+2] cycloaddition between the ruthenium alkylidene catalyst [Ru=CHR] and an alkene monomer.

options.label: C
options.text: A four-membered dioxetane ring.

options.label: D
options.text: A ruthenium cyclopentadienyl sandwich complex.

questions.correct_answer: A metallacyclobutane intermediate formed by reversible [2+2] cycloaddition between the ruthenium alkylidene catalyst [Ru=CHR] and an alkene monomer.

questions.question: Why is Ring-Closing Metathesis (RCM) of α,ω-dienes thermodynamically favored to form cyclic alkenes?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction releases elemental chlorine gas.

options.label: B
options.text: The intramolecular cyclization expels a molecule of gaseous ethylene (CH₂=CH₂ ↑), which bubbles out of solution, providing an irreversible entropic driving force (ΔS° > 0).

options.label: C
options.text: Cyclic alkenes are always more stable than linear dienes.

options.label: D
options.text: Ruthenium is permanently consumed as a solid product.

questions.question: What mechanistic pathway explains the selective 1,4-addition of lithium dialkylcuprates (R₂CuLi) to conjugated enones?

options.label: A
options.text: Single-electron transfer and coordination of copper to the enone π system followed by migratory insertion at the β-carbon and reductive elimination.

options.label: C

questions.question: How is dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) generated from chloroform (CHCl₃) and potassium tert-butoxide?

questions.question: What is the correct sequential order of elementary steps in the palladium-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling?

options.label: A
options.text: Oxidative addition of Pd(0) into aryl halide → Transmetalation of organoboronic acid to Pd(II) → Reductive elimination of biaryl product regenerating Pd(0).

options.label: B
options.text: Transmetalation → Oxidative addition → Reductive elimination.

options.label: C
options.text: Reductive elimination → Migratory insertion → Beta-elimination.

questions.correct_answer: Oxidative addition of Pd(0) into aryl halide → Transmetalation of organoboronic acid to Pd(II) → Reductive elimination of biaryl product regenerating Pd(0).
questions.explanation: The Suzuki catalytic cycle comprises three core organometallic steps: oxidative addition, base-assisted transmetalation, and reductive elimination.

questions.topic: Suzuki Coupling Base Role in Transmetalation
questions.question: What is the crucial role of the base (e.g., Na₂CO₃ or NaOH) in the Suzuki-Miyaura coupling?

options.label: A
options.text: Base deprotonates the aryl halide.

options.label: B
options.text: Base oxidizes Pd(0) to Pd(II).

options.label: C
options.text: Base precipitates palladium as a solid mirror.

options.label: D
options.text: Base coordinates to the boron atom of the boronic acid to form an anionic boronate complex [Ar-B(OH)₃⁻], which activates the organic group for transmetalation to palladium.

questions.correct_answer: Base coordinates to the boron atom of the boronic acid to form an anionic boronate complex [Ar-B(OH)₃⁻], which activates the organic group for transmetalation to palladium.

options.text: Radical coupling in solution.

options.label: C
options.text: Backside SN2 attack of palladium on the double bond.

options.label: D
options.text: Syn migratory insertion of the alkene into the Pd-Ar bond followed by C-C bond rotation and syn β-hydride elimination to form the thermodynamically favored trans-cinnamate.

questions.correct_answer: Syn migratory insertion of the alkene into the Pd-Ar bond followed by C-C bond rotation and syn β-hydride elimination to form the thermodynamically favored trans-cinnamate.
questions.explanation: Both migratory insertion and β-hydride elimination are strictly syn processes; internal rotation to align Pd and H syn delivers the trans-alkene.
